title: Mantle cell lymphoma
subtitle: CD5+, cyclin D1+ B-cell lymphoma driven by t(11;14) · a spectrum from observable leukemic non-nodal disease to blastoid disease · TP53 status, Ki-67 and fitness — not stage — choose the therapy; BTK inhibitors have displaced routine ASCT
source: Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Lymphoma: Non-Hodgkin — mantle cell (Chou L, Schroers-Martin J, Gupta NK) · NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas v4.2026 · primary trial reports and FDA actions verified against PubMed, September 2026.

blocks.heading: Diagnosis
items: Hallmark: t(11;14)(q13;q32), IGH::CCND1 → cyclin D1 overexpression — show it by cyclin D1 IHC or FISH
Phenotype: CD5+, CD20 bright, CD23−, CD10−, cyclin D1+, SOX11+. CD23 negativity and cyclin D1 separate it from CLL, which is CD5+ CD23+
Cyclin D1-negative MCL is real: SOX11+, with a CCND2 rearrangement in ~55%. Diagnose it on SOX11 + morphology; treat as MCL Salaverria, Blood 2013
SOX11 does double duty — rescues the cyclin D1-negative diagnosis, and its absence flags the indolent leukemic non-nodal form

blocks.heading: The spectrum — WHO-HAEM5 / ICC 2022
rows: SOX11+, IGHV mostly unmutated; nodes + marrow, spleen, GI tract (lymphomatous polyposis). Chronic relapsing course
SOX11−, IGHV-mutated, blood + marrow ± spleen, no significant adenopathy. Indolent: 5-yr OS 78% vs 36% for SOX11+ Fernàndez 2010 — observe unless it acquires TP53 or goes nodal
High Ki-67, TP53 enriched, CNS-prone. Treat as high risk; blastoid adds nothing to prognosis once Ki-67 is known
Cyclin D1+ cells confined to mantle zones of a reactive node — usually incidental; stage and observe

blocks.heading: Workup
items: PET/CT, marrow biopsy with flow and t(11;14) FISH, CBC with smear (leukemic phase), LDH, β2-microglobulin, HBV serology before anti-CD20
TP53 by NGS (+ del(17p) FISH) and Ki-67 at diagnosis in every patient — they pick the regimen, not the stage
EGD + colonoscopy for apparent stage I–II (to confirm limited disease) and when GI symptoms
LP / brain MRI if blastoid or neurologic symptoms. Echo before anthracycline

blocks.heading: Pearls
items: CD5+ CD23− small B cells = send cyclin D1. If cyclin D1− but SOX11+, it is still MCL
Send TP53 before choosing. A TP53-mutant patient gets little from cytarabine + ASCT
Rituximab maintenance is standard in MCL after both intensive and BR induction — unlike follicular, LyMa showed an OS gain at 4 yr (attenuated by 7)
No BTKi-added frontline trial in older patients has shown OS gain (SHINE, ECHO) — PFS gain costs toxicity
Brexu-cel is the most active post-BTKi therapy but the most neurotoxic; liso-cel trades a little efficacy for much less CRS/ICANS

blocks.heading: MIPI — add the points
blocks.footnote: Low 0–3 (44%; median OS not reached) · intermediate 4–5 (35%; 51 mo) · high 6–11 (21%; 29 mo). Hoster, Blood 2008 — pre-BTKi survival; use it to stratify, not to counsel.

blocks.heading: Biology that overrides the score
items: TP53 mutation is the dominant adverse factor. 11% in Nordic MCL2/3 Median OS 1.8 vs 12.7 yr, OS HR 6.2; half relapsed within a year of cytarabine induction + ASCT Eskelund, Blood 2017
Ki-67 ≥30% is the validated cutoff. MIPI-c = MIPI group + Ki-67 → 4 groups, 5-yr OS 85% / 72% / 43% / 17% Hoster, JCO 2016
Blastoid/pleomorphic cytology, complex karyotype, del(17p) travel with TP53 and high Ki-67

blocks.html: Watch and wait is legitimate for selected patients — leukemic non-nodal SOX11− disease, or asymptomatic classic MCL with low burden, low Ki-67 and wild-type TP53. In a Weill Cornell series 32% were observed; median time to treatment 12 mo (range 4–128), with no survival penalty (a selected cohort) Martin, JCO 2009.

ASCT in first remission is no longer default. Its PFS benefit predates BTKi and maintenance. TRIANGLE: adding ASCT to ibrutinib gave no FFS gain and more toxicity. EA4151: in MRD-negative CR, ASCT + rituximab = rituximab alone (abstract only).

blocks.heading: Chemo-immunotherapy — infection and supportive care
items: Bendamustine is deeply immunosuppressive — prolonged CD4 lymphopenia: PJP (TMP-SMX) + VZV (acyclovir) prophylaxis; ECHO grade 5 COVID-19 9.4% vs 6.7%. Rash with allopurinol
Rituximab maintenance → hypogammaglobulinemia and infection; check IgG, replace if recurrent infections. HBV prophylaxis if core Ab+
Lenalidomide: aspirin or anticoagulant VTE prophylaxis, renal dose adjustment

boxes: leukemic non-nodal, or low Ki-67 asymptomatic
older standard: Nordic or R-DHAP → ASCT → R q2mo ×3 yr
pirtobrutinib — bridge, or if CAR-T not possible
allo-HCT if fit · trials (bispecifics, BTK degraders)

pages.subtitle: Page 2 — the evidence (frontline by fitness; relapsed disease by agent and approval status), regimen dosing and toxicity

blocks.heading: Frontline evidence
rows: Ibrutinib + ASCT (A+I) beat ASCT alone (A): 3-yr FFS 88% vs 72%, HR 0.52. At 4.5 yr A+I not better than ibrutinib without ASCT (I): 4-yr FFS 82% vs 81%. 4-yr OS 88–90% vs 81% for either ibrutinib arm vs A (HR 0.57–0.59)
Primary endpoint is FFS. Maintenance grade 3–5 heme toxicity 54% A+I vs 28% I. Uses ibrutinib, which has no US MCL label; applying it to acalabrutinib/zanubrutinib is extrapolation
Rituximab maintenance on top of ibrutinib: 4-yr PFS 85% vs 73% (arm I)
R-DHAP → ASCT → rituximab q2mo ×3 yr vs observation: 4-yr EFS 79% vs 61%, OS 89% vs 80% (HR 0.50)
PFS gain holds at 7 yr (HR 0.36); OS gain no longer significant
ASCT + R maintenance vs R maintenance alone: 3-yr OS 82.1% vs 82.7% (HR 1.11); PFS 76.6% vs 77.4%. Crossed futility
Maxi-R-CHOP / R-high-dose cytarabine → ASCT: median PFS 8.5 yr, OS 12.7 yr
Ibrutinib + BR → R maintenance: median PFS 80.6 vs 52.9 mo (HR 0.75)
No OS benefit — excess adverse-event deaths; AF 13.9% vs 6.5%
Acalabrutinib + BR: median PFS 66.4 vs 49.6 mo (HR 0.73). Regular FDA approval, Jan 2025
No OS difference (HR 0.86). AF 6.7% vs 4.4%; grade 5 COVID-19 9.4% vs 6.7%
Ibrutinib + rituximab vs R-chemo: PFS HR 0.69. vs R-CHOP HR 0.37; vs BR HR 0.91 (NS)
Chemo-free BTKi-R matches BR and beats R-CHOP
Bortezomib for vincristine in R-CHOP: PFS 24.7 vs 14.4 mo; median OS 90.7 vs 55.7 mo (HR 0.66)
The one older-patient trial with an OS gain
Missed its safety boundary: 72% dose-reduced, grade 3–4 cytopenias in ~half of cycles
Zanubrutinib + obinutuzumab + venetoclax: ORR 96%, CR 88%, 2-yr PFS 72%
Single-arm phase 2 — the best TP53 data, not yet randomized

blocks.heading: Relapsed / refractory — agents and status (Sept 2026)
rows: BGB-3111-206 (n=86): ORR 84%, CR 69%, median PFS 22.1 mo
Pivotal single-arm data; SHINE did not confirm
SYMPATICO (n=267): median PFS 31.9 vs 22.1 mo, HR 0.65 vs ibrutinib
Not approved as a combination in MCL
BRUIN, after covalent BTKi (n=90): ORR 58%, CR 20%, median DOR 21.6 mo; grade ≥3 AF 1.2%
Accelerated (Jan 2023; ≥2 lines incl. BTKi). Confirmatory BRUIN MCL-321 not yet reported
ZUMA-2: ORR 93%, CR 67%; 3-yr median PFS 25.8 mo, OS 46.6 mo. Grade ≥3 CRS 15%, neurologic events 31%
TRANSCEND MCL (n=83): ORR 83%, CR 72%, median PFS 15.3 mo. Grade 3–4 CRS 1%, neurologic 9%
Phase 2 (n=103), post-BTKi: ORR 52%, CR 16%, median PFS 6.5 mo; TP53-mut ORR 59%; TLS 7%
Phase 1/2 (n=60): ORR 85%, CR 78% (71% after BTKi); CRS 70%
Not approved in MCL (US or EU) — phase 3 GLOBRYTE pending
SPRINT: PFS 8.7 vs 5.2 mo vs investigator choice (HR 0.61); EMERGE post-bortezomib ORR 28%
Only curative-intent option after CAR-T failure
blocks.footnote: Relapse after frontline BTKi (TRIANGLE, ECHO) is now common: those patients are BTKi-exposed at first relapse, so the post-BTKi column is effectively second line. Response to a covalent BTKi at relapse after BTKi-containing induction is not established.

blocks.heading: Regimen dosing
rows: R-CHOP + ibrutinib: rituximab 375, cyclophosphamide 750, doxorubicin 50, vincristine 1.4 (max 2 mg) d1, prednisone 100 mg d1–5 + ibrutinib 560 mg d1–19, alternating with R-DHAP (rituximab 375, dexamethasone 40 mg d1–4, cytarabine 2 g/m² q12h ×2 d2, cisplatin 100 CIV d1) or R-DHAOx (oxaliplatin 130) — q21d ×6. Then ibrutinib 560 mg daily ×2 yr ± rituximab
R-DHAP q21d ×4 → ASCT → rituximab 375 q2 months ×3 yr
Rituximab 375 d1 + bendamustine 90 d1–2, q28d ×6 → rituximab 375 q8wk ×2 yr. ECHO adds acalabrutinib 100 mg BID until progression
Rituximab 375, cyclophosphamide 750, doxorubicin 50 d1; bortezomib 1.3 d1, 4, 8, 11; prednisone 100 d1–5 — q21d ×6
Rituximab 375 d1, bendamustine 70 d2–3, cytarabine 500 d2–4 — q28d, up to 6
Lenalidomide 20 mg d1–21 q28d + rituximab 375 weekly ×4 (cycle 1), then per protocol. VTE prophylaxis
Ibrutinib 560 mg daily · acalabrutinib 100 mg BID · zanubrutinib 160 mg BID or 320 mg daily · pirtobrutinib 200 mg daily — continuous
Brexu-cel: flu 30 + cy 500 mg/m² d−5 to −3, then 2×106 CAR-T cells/kg (max 2×108). Liso-cel: flu 30 + cy 300 mg/m² ×3 d, then 90–110×106 CAR+ T cells. Avoid bendamustine shortly before apheresis
blocks.footnote: mg/m² unless stated. Cytarabine: prednisolone 1% eye drops from 12 h before to 48 h after; reduce to 1 g/m² if age >60; hold for rising creatinine (cerebellar toxicity).

blocks.heading: Targeted and cellular therapy — toxicity
items: BTKi class: atrial fibrillation, bleeding, hypertension, infection, plus arthralgia, diarrhea, rash. Hold 3–7 days around procedures; avoid warfarin; watch CYP3A interactions

Second-generation agents cut AF by about half: ELEVATE-RR (CLL) 9.4% acalabrutinib vs 16.0% ibrutinib; ALPINE fewer cardiac events with zanubrutinib; in MCL, ECHO 6.7% vs SHINE 13.9% (cross-trial). Acalabrutinib: early headache. Zanubrutinib: neutropenia. Pirtobrutinib: grade ≥3 AF ~1%

CAR-T: CRS → tocilizumab ± dexamethasone; ICANS → dexamethasone (tocilizumab only if CRS coexists), levetiracetam. Brexu-cel is the more neurotoxic (grade ≥3 neuro 31% vs 9% liso-cel). Late: cytopenias, hypogammaglobulinemia, boxed warning for T-cell malignancy
Venetoclax / sonrotoclax: TLS — MCL can be bulky and leukemic; ramp-up, hydration, allopurinol, lab checks at each step
